question: Will Perry Johnson win the 2026 Michigan Governor Republican primary election?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Republican Primary for Governor of Michigan, scheduled to take place on August 4, 2026. Resolution will be based on the overall winner of the primary, including any potential second round or run-off.

If no 2026 Michigan Gubernatorial Republican Primary takes place, this market will resolve to “Other.”

The resolution source for this market will be the first official announcement of the results from the Michigan Republican Party; however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.publisher: Michigan Advance / News From The States
evidence.excerpt: Team Trump criticized Perry Johnson for promoting a planned “Trump Tailgate” despite lacking the president’s endorsement. John James was the Trump-endorsed candidate in the Republican gubernatorial primary. Johnson responded that he loved and supported Trump while criticizing the advice behind the James endorsement.

The Washington Reporter published internal polling from Mike Cox’s campaign conducted by co/efficient shortly before Cox withdrew. It showed John James at 36%, Perry Johnson at 23%, and Cox at 21%. The article reported that James’s ballot share and image were relatively unchanged despite more than $5 million in advertising directed against him since Trump’s endorsement.

Former Michigan Attorney General Mike Cox withdrew from the Republican gubernatorial race and endorsed John James, leaving James and Perry Johnson as the two active candidates. Cox said internal polls after Trump’s June 22 endorsement showed James out of reach in a three-way primary. Cox and Aric Nesbitt would remain on the already printed primary ballot despite ending their campaigns.

evidence.publisher: Michigan Public / Michigan Public Radio Network
evidence.excerpt: John James, Perry Johnson, and Mike Cox participated in a televised gubernatorial debate in Grand Rapids on July 9 ahead of the August 4 Republican primary. Michigan Public reported that James had consistently led polling, aided partly by Trump’s endorsement. Johnson, who had largely financed his own campaign, presented that self-funding as a source of independence.

A Mitchell Research & Communications survey conducted June 11–13 for MIRS found John James at 28%, Mike Cox at 27%, Perry Johnson at 23%, and Aric Nesbitt at 4%, with 18% undecided. The survey covered 404 likely August Republican primary voters. The June 15 release described Johnson as within the poll’s margin of error of the leaders.

The official candidate list, updated May 29, 2026, lists Perry Johnson, John James, Mike Cox, and Aric Nesbitt as Republican candidates for governor. The gubernatorial contest is designated a four-year term with voters instructed to vote for no more than one candidate.

Perry Johnson announced another Michigan gubernatorial campaign ahead of the August 4 primary. His 2022 bid ended over insufficient valid petition signatures, and he also pursued the 2024 presidency. Johnson planned to spend $9 million personally within two months; incumbent Governor Gretchen Whitmer was term-limited.
